questions.q: What excites most Bitcoin investors, according to the summary?
a: The story of a revolutionary, government-free future
The complex mathematics behind the ledger
The promise of steady, low-risk returns
The backing of major central banks
questions.why: Lesson 1 says futuristic narratives and Bitcoin's mysterious origins attracted investors more than the math.

questions.q: What did Shiller compare economic narratives to?
a: Contagious epidemics that spread, peak and fade
Lotteries that reward a lucky few
Machines that run without human input
Laws that apply evenly to every market
questions.why: Lesson 2 draws a parallel between narrative contagion and the spread curves of diseases like Ebola.

questions.q: What pattern did news mentions of Bitcoin follow?
a: Sharp peaks and declines, like an epidemic curve
A slow, steady rise with no setbacks
A flat line after the first year
A decline that never recovered
questions.why: Lesson 2 notes a sharp rise in 2014, another peak in 2018 and a fall, resembling an epidemic graph.

questions.q: Why did Roosevelt's fireside chats matter economically?
a: They calmed fear and markets stabilized after each talk
They announced new taxes on the wealthy
They replaced Congress as a lawmaking body
They convinced banks to stop lending
questions.why: Lesson 3 says Roosevelt understood that lost confidence was hurting the economy and asked people to spend.

questions.q: How can policymakers use narratives, according to the summary?
a: By shaping people's behavior in times of stress
By hiding bad news from the public
By banning stories that spread panic
By letting markets correct themselves
questions.why: Lesson 3 argues that understanding narratives lets policy-makers shape behavior during stressful periods.
